subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Eta Carinae: A Ticking Time Bomb
description: A short lesson to help you apply Eta Carinae: A Ticking Time Bomb.

hook.text: Eta Carinae is 5 million times brighter than the Sun and dangerously unstable. It could explode at any time.

buildup.text: In 1843, it erupted so violently it became the second-brightest star in the sky—without actually exploding.

discovery.text: The eruption ejected 10 solar masses of material, forming the Homunculus Nebula—two glowing lobes around the star.

twist.text: Eta Carinae is actually two stars orbiting each other. Their winds collide at millions of degrees.

climax.text: When it finally goes supernova, it may produce a gamma-ray burst—one of the most energetic events possible.

punchline.text: Already erupted once. The real explosion hasn't happened yet.

quiz.question: What happened during Eta Carinae's Great Eruption in 1843?
options: It ejected massive amounts of material without actually exploding as a supernova
It collapsed into a black hole that is still growing
It split into two separate stars

details.summary: Eta Carinae is one of the most massive and luminous stars known — roughly 100 solar masses and 5 million times the Sun's luminosity. In the 1840s, it erupted in a massive explosion, becoming the second-brightest star despite being 7,500 light-years away.
details.whyItMatters: Eta Carinae represents the most extreme stellar behavior astronomers can study. Its impending death will be one of the most energetic events in our galaxy's recent history, potentially producing a hypernova.
takeaways: Eta Carinae has about 100 solar masses and extreme luminosity
It erupted massively in the 1840s, becoming very bright
It may explode as a hypernova in astronomical timescales

faq.question: What happened during the Great Eruption?
faq.answer: In the 1840s, Eta Carinae ejected roughly 10-40 solar masses of material, briefly becoming one of the brightest stars in the sky. The ejected material formed the Homunculus Nebula — a bipolar cloud still expanding around the star. The eruption's cause remains debated.

faq.question: What is a hypernova?
faq.answer: A hypernova is an exceptionally energetic supernova, at least 10 times more powerful than a standard supernova. They may produce gamma-ray bursts — the most energetic events in the universe. Eta Carinae's extreme mass makes it a possible hypernova candidate.
